cards.text: Israel's king, Joram son of Ahab, is back in Jezreel healing from wounds he took fighting Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead (2 Kings 8:28-29). Now Elisha the prophet calls one of the sons of the prophets over and says, "Tuck your cloak under your belt, take this flask of oil, and go to Ramoth-gilead." Friend, I don't know what that oil's for yet, but nobody tucks up their cloak to walk SLOW.

cards.question: Elisha tells the young man who to look for once he gets to Ramoth-gilead. Who is it?

cards.text: Elisha says to go in and get Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi (not Judah's King Jehoshaphat), away from his companions. Whatever this is, friend, it is NOT a group announcement.

cards.question: Once the young prophet gets Jehu away from his companions, where does Elisha tell him to take Jehu?

cards.text: Next step, Elisha says: pour the oil right on Jehu's head and speak the LORD's words. Friend, I get nervous asking someone to pass the sprinkles, and this young man has to walk up and pour oil on somebody's HEAD.

cards.question: Elisha says that with the oil on Jehu's head, the young prophet is to speak for the LORD and say He anoints Jehu ___ over Israel.
Elisha tells the young prophet that once he anoints Jehu, he should stay and wait for Jehu's answer.

cards.text: So the young prophet heads to Ramoth-gilead and walks in on the army commanders, all sitting there together. He says he has a message for the commander, which is like walking into a room FULL of managers and asking to speak to the manager.

cards.question: When the young prophet says he has a message for the commander, Jehu asks which of them it's for.

cards.text: "For you, commander," comes the answer, so Jehu goes into the house, and there the oil goes on his head with the LORD's word: "I anoint you king over the LORD’s people Israel." Friend, Jehu didn't apply, didn't interview, didn't even get a heads-up, and he just got the BIGGEST promotion in the country.

cards.question: The LORD gives Jehu a job: strike down the house of his master. Whose house is it?

cards.text: Ahab was Israel's king before his son Joram (1 Kings 16:29; 2 Kings 8:16), and the LORD calls him Jehu's master.

cards.question: What reason does the LORD give Jehu for striking down Ahab's house?

answers.text: To avenge the blood of His prophets
To return the throne to David's family
To make room for a new temple

cards.text: That blood, and the blood of all the servants of the LORD, was shed by the hand of Jezebel, Ahab's wife (1 Kings 16:31). I think this one hurts, friend.

The LORD says the whole house of Ahab will perish, and He will cut off from Ahab every male in Israel, slave and free. He'll make Ahab's house like the houses of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah, earlier kings of Israel whose houses were struck down (1 Kings 15:29; 16:11).

cards.question: Then the LORD speaks about Jezebel. He says someone will give her a proper burial.

cards.text: On the plot of ground at Jezreel, the LORD says, the dogs will devour Jezebel. Then the young prophet opens the door and runs, just like Elisha said.

cards.question: Jehu walks back out, and his master's servants ask if everything is all right. What do they call the young prophet?

cards.text: A madman, they call him, and they want to know why he came to Jehu. Friend, a guy pours oil on a commander's head and RUNS out the door, so I kind of see how they got there.

cards.question: When the servants ask why the madman came, how does Jehu answer them at first?

answers.text: He brushes it off as prophet babble
He says the man had the wrong commander
He says the man came asking for money

cards.text: The servants aren't buying it, and they fire right back: "That is a lie!" and "Tell us now!" That's the exact look I get when I swear I only tasted ONE cookie.
So Jehu comes clean. He tells them the prophet said, "This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel."

cards.question: Quickly, each man takes his ___ and puts it under Jehu on the bare steps.
Then the men proclaim Jehu king.

cards.text: They blow the ram's horn and proclaim, "Jehu is king!" Hold on to your apron, friend, because this story is still in the oven.
